docling.notes: High-fidelity PDF/Office conversion (tables, layout, OCR), converted locally (docling-mcp 3.x defaults to a remote service; the [local] extra plus DOCLING_MCP_CONVERSION_MODE=local keeps files on this machine). First run downloads packages and models (~1-2 GB).

playwright.notes: Scripted browser automation (forms, logins, JS-heavy pages) when WebFetch/Jina/Spider are not enough. Headless, in-memory profile (parallel instances don't fight over a profile lock); uses Google Chrome — without it: npx @playwright/mcp@0.0.82 install-browser chrome.

lean.notes: Lean 4 proof assistant via LSP. Needs a Lean toolchain (elan) and a built Lake project (lake build); LEAN_PROJECT_PATH is recommended (optional over stdio).

docspace.notes: ONLYOFFICE DocSpace (cloud rooms/files). Requires a DocSpace account and OAuth. magg cannot expand ${VAR} in headers, so never put an API key here: for regular use add it to Claude Code instead — claude mcp add --transport http docspace https://mcp.onlyoffice.com/mcp — and sign in with /mcp.

duckdb.notes: SQL over local files (CSV/Parquet/JSON) and DuckDB databases through an in-memory DuckDB; ATTACH or switch to a .duckdb file by absolute path. MotherDuck cloud needs motherduck_token and --db-path md:.

arxiv.notes: arXiv search, download and full-text reading of papers (stored under ~/.arxiv-mcp-server/papers; the [pdf] extra reads older papers that have no arXiv HTML). Jina's search_arxiv covers quick lookups; mount this for deep paper work.

jupyter.notes: Drive a running JupyterLab/Jupyter Server kernel (execute cells, read outputs). Needs JUPYTER_URL and JUPYTER_TOKEN in stack.env and a server the user started with jupyterlab, jupyter-collaboration, jupyter-mcp-tools and ipykernel installed; NotebookEdit alone does not execute cells.

mlflow.notes: MLflow trace search and management for LLM/agent evaluation. Needs MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI in stack.env (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:5000 or a file:// store). --no-project keeps uv from creating a .venv/uv.lock in your project.

mongodb.notes: Official MongoDB server: find, aggregate, explain, list collections and indexes, schema sampling. Read-only (--readOnly registers no create/update/delete tools); telemetry off. Needs MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING in stack.env (a local or dev database; never production without the user's word), or the connect tool with a string the user gave.

postgres.notes: Postgres MCP Pro: schema listing, read-only SQL, EXPLAIN plans, index tuning advice, database health checks. --access-mode=restricted runs read-only transactions with execution-time limits. Needs DATABASE_URI (postgresql://user:pass@host:5432/db) in stack.env. psql through Bash does the same for anything scripted.

ros.notes: ROS 1/ROS 2 over rosbridge (WebSocket, default port 9090): discover topics, services, actions and their types; subscribe, publish, call services, set parameters. The robot side runs rosbridge_server (ros2 launch rosbridge_server rosbridge_websocket_launch.xml). Its tools can MOVE a real robot: they are not pre-approved, so each call asks the user; use a simulator unless the user says otherwise.

chrome-devtools.notes: Chrome DevTools from Google: performance traces and insights, Lighthouse audits, network requests, console messages, CSS, heap snapshots, emulation. Headless, throwaway profile, no usage statistics, no CrUX lookups (page URLs stay local). Needs Google Chrome.

qiskit-runtime.notes: IBM Quantum Platform through Qiskit Runtime: list backends and their calibration, submit and monitor jobs on real hardware, fetch results. Needs QISKIT_IBM_TOKEN in stack.env. Hardware jobs spend the account's quota: its tools are not pre-approved, so each call asks the user. Simulate locally first (qiskit-aer).
